# Agentronics

> Agentronics makes company websites ready for AI agents. It scores how well AI agents can use your site (the Agent Readiness Score, 0–100), then Agent Nic, our AI agent, fixes the problems in a GitHub pull request you approve.

## Key facts

- Agent Readiness Score: free, about 30 seconds, no signup. 12 checks in three groups: Find, Read, Act. Reads public pages only.
- Score bands: 0–40 Not ready · 41–70 Partly ready · 71–100 Agent-ready.
- Agent Nic: writes fixes (labels, structured data, sitemap, llms.txt, agent actions) and opens a pull request. Nothing changes until you click Merge. Included in every plan, including Free.
- Control: allow, ask first or deny each agent action. See which agents visit. Alerts when a code change breaks agent access.
- Your site looks the same to people. Agents see the same content people see (no cloaking).

## Pricing (USD, monthly or yearly; yearly saves 21%)

- Free: $0. 1 site, 1 fix round/month, up to 5 agent actions, 5,000 agent visits/month.
- Starter: $19/month or $180/year (most popular). 5 fix rounds, up to 15 actions, automatic fixes + alerts on code changes, agent verification, 5 access rules.
- Pro: $49/month or $465/year. 3 sites, 30 fix rounds, unlimited actions, unlimited rules + rate limits.
- Enterprise: custom. Unlimited sites, SSO/SAML, audit log, SLA.

## Agent actions

- Scan API: `GET https://www.agentronics.dev/api/scan?url=example.com` returns the score as JSON. [OpenAPI](https://www.agentronics.dev/openapi.json)
- WebMCP: the scan form is declared as the tool `get_agent_readiness_score`; `get_pricing` returns plans.

## Developers

- [SDK overview](https://www.agentronics.dev/developers): WebMCP tools, detection, authentication, authorization, procedural memory, observability.
- [Docs](https://www.agentronics.dev/docs) and the [quickstart](https://www.agentronics.dev/docs/getting-started): install @agentronics/sdk and publish a governed WebMCP tool.
